title: Telemetry for Dedicated staged rollout gates: queue depth, pool utilization, timeout rate (low-cardinality)
creator: Logan Wright
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Problem
Dedicated staged rollouts require robust, low-latency telemetry for gate evaluation. Today, we have partial signals (request latency/error metrics) but we are missing Dedicated-pool-specific metrics (queue depth, utilization/headroom, timeout rate) and some of the existing metrics have label sets that are too high-cardinality to be safely queried at scale during rollouts.

This ticket adds/standardizes the required metrics so the gate evaluator (ENG-5124) can reliably query per-pool health and enforce “stop-the-line” behavior.

Scope (what we are adding)
1) Dedicated pool queue depth metric
- Name: redwood_dedicated_pool_queue_depth
- Type: gauge
- Meaning: number of queued inference requests waiting for a worker slot in a Dedicated reserved pool.
- Required labels (low-card): tenant_id, pool_id, region
- Notes: pool_id cardinality is bounded by # dedicated pools; acceptable for gating. Do NOT include route_id, request_id, model_id.

2) Dedicated pool GPU utilization metric
- Name: redwood_dedicated_pool_gpu_utilization_ratio
- Type: gauge (0.0–1.0)
- Meaning: rolling 30s average utilization across GPUs in the pool (defined by “active SM utilization” from the node exporter / fleet agent).
- Required labels: tenant_id, pool_id, region
- Notes: if per-node utilization exists, we will aggregate to pool-level before export to avoid node_id label.

3) Timeout rate for Dedicated pools
- Names:
  - redwood_dedicated_pool_requests_total (counter)
  - redwood_dedicated_pool_request_timeouts_total (counter)
- Labels (requests_total): tenant_id, pool_id, region, outcome
  - outcome is an enum: success | error_5xx | error_4xx | timeout
- Labels (request_timeouts_total): tenant_id, pool_id, region, timeout_type
  - timeout_type is an enum: queue_timeout | upstream_timeout | inference_timeout
- Gate evaluator query pattern: timeout_rate = rate(request_timeouts_total[5m]) / rate(requests_total[5m])
- Notes: avoid status_code, grpc_status, and exception labels for this path; they are too explosive.

4) Metrics freshness / ingestion delay (supporting gate evaluator “fail safe”)
- Name: redwood_metrics_pipeline_ingest_lag_seconds
- Type: gauge
- Labels: pipeline (enum: otel-collector | remote-write | backend)
- Purpose: allow evaluator + SRE dashboards to detect “metrics are lying / late” and hold rollouts.

Cardinality rules (must-have)
- Allowlist label sets for any metric used by gates.
- Explicitly prohibited labels on gate metrics: request_id, trace_id, route_id (unless we can prove bounded), model_id, model_version, rollout_id, stage_id, pod_name, node_id.
- If we need split-by-variant for future A/B: use a small enum label (traffic_group: baseline | candidate) emitted by routing, NOT rollout_id.

Acceptance criteria
- Metrics present in staging and prod for Dedicated pools, with documented definitions and example queries.
- Gate evaluator can compute the following per (tenant_id, pool_id) over 5m windows:
  - p95 latency (existing; validate label set)
  - 5xx rate (existing; validate label set)
  - timeout_rate (new)
  - avg queue depth and/or max queue depth (new)
  - utilization ratio (new)
- Cardinality check: top-20 series count for each new metric is within expectations; no accidental high-card labels.
- Freshness: for the main gate metrics, 99% of samples arrive within 60s in staging under load test conditions.
- Links provided to dashboards/alerts spec (ENG-5131) so SRE can validate.

Implementation plan (high level)
- Instrument Dedicated scheduler / queue manager to emit pool_queue_depth gauge.
- Export pool-level utilization from fleet agent (aggregate node stats -> pool).
- Standardize “outcome” + “timeout_type” enums in router / gateway metrics.
- Add label validation tests (unit) + a CI check that rejects forbidden labels for the gate metric names.
- Update internal metrics catalog entry + add example PromQL snippets for evaluator.

Risks / notes
- Pool_id is inherently “per-tenant object” and will grow, but is still bounded. We should be careful with additional dimensions.
- Utilization is often noisy; recommend evaluator uses an evaluation window >= 5m and does not gate on utilization alone (combine with queue depth / timeouts).
- Missing metrics must be treated as “unknown => hold” by evaluator (ENG-5124); this ticket must ensure we can detect missingness via ingest lag + “series absent” alerts.

comments: 2025-01-10 (Logan Wright): Creating this as a blocker for gate evaluator. We need Dedicated-pool-native signals (queue depth, utilization, timeout rate) with strict label hygiene. Biggest risk is accidental per-route/per-version labels during rollouts.

2025-01-13 (Paula Mendes): For beta, default gates are latency/5xx/timeout/queue depth. Utilization is helpful but should not be the only gate. Please make sure we can compute timeout_rate cleanly without relying on status_code labels.

2025-01-16 (Thomas Baird): +1 on label hygiene. We should explicitly forbid stage_id/rollout_id labels. If we need variant comparison later, use a small traffic_group enum (baseline/candidate) and only emit when enabled for Dedicated rollouts.

2025-01-22 (Caleb Johnson): Spike in staging: we can export queue depth from scheduler, but current gateway metrics include route_id which explodes series count for high-traffic tenants. Plan: new dedicated_* metrics will not include route_id; we’ll keep route-level metrics separate for debugging only.

2025-02-03 (Caleb Johnson): Implemented telemetry plumbing and exported redwood_dedicated_pool_queue_depth + redwood_dedicated_pool_requests_total + request_timeouts_total. PR up: pr_28503. Added outcome/timeout_type enums; removed raw status_code on the gate path.

2025-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): SRE review: looks good, but we need an ingest lag metric and an alert when series go absent for a pool under active rollout. Please coordinate with ENG-5131; evaluator should treat missing as HOLD.

2025-02-07 (Caleb Johnson): Added redwood_metrics_pipeline_ingest_lag_seconds and a lightweight “series absent” recording rule doc snippet for dashboards. Also found accidental label "pod" in utilization path; removed by aggregating to pool-level in fleet agent.

2025-02-10 (Logan Wright): Follow-up landed to reduce cardinality across rollout/gate metrics and enforce forbidden labels. PR: pr_28640. This should prevent regressions where per-route labels sneak back into gate queries.

2025-02-13 (Allison Grant): Verified the new metrics show up cleanly in staging dashboards and remain stable under the load test scenario. Marking Done; remaining dashboard wiring tracked in ENG-5131.
